analysis.title: DeskTalk - Oil sinks as Iran tone eases
key_insights: Oil fell nearly 9% in a knee-jerk move as Washington messaging on Iran shifted toward de-escalation. Brent broke below $100 and $95 and is at levels last seen in early October.

US VP Vance said voter frustration over the Iran war and the US-Israel relationship was the reason for the Democrats' landslide victory at the midterms. Senate Minority Leader Schumer said the Iran war 'must end' and that some Republicans have joined Democrats.

Citi says support for de-escalation is turning bipartisan, which supports further correction in oil. Foreign policy stays in the executive branch and Trump has veto authority, but a two-thirds Senate majority with Republican backing could let Congress constrain or pause military action.

Citi macro strategist Jim McCormick said the midterm results raised the probability of de-escalation. His preferred expression is receiving front-end EUR rates. Selling front-end European inflation is also good for those willing to take more risk, though Citi says that is purely a long/short gas trade.
Citi's energy strategist said the short-term outlook could stay choppy until official confirmation or a deal, while the longer-term outlook for energy markets remains bearish.

Across assets, treasuries returned to overnight high levels, the equity rally is stalling, and gold is up about 3.5%. Citi says a meaningful de-escalation would likely move markets beyond geopolitics and back to fundamentals.
